utterances.text: I am a student at the moment. [pause 0.4 s] I study engineering at a college in the city. [pause 0.6 s] It is hard work but I enjoy it.
Most days I ride my bicycle. [pause 0.4 s] It takes about twenty minutes. [pause 0.8 s] When it rains I take the train instead.
Yes I love music. [pause 0.6 s] I have played the violin since I was eight years old. [pause 0.4 s] I practice every evening after dinner.

I want to talk about a train journey I took last spring. [pause 0.4 s] I traveled from my hometown to the coast with my cousin. [pause 0.4 s] We left very early in the morning. [pause 0.9 s] The train was full of families going on holiday. [pause 0.4 s] Through the window, we could see farms and small villages. [pause 0.6 s] In [withheld for audio check] was shining. [pause 0.4 s] We went straight to the beach and had an ice cream.

[pause 0.9 s] My cousin had brought a camera and took photos of everything. [pause 0.9 s] In the afternoon, we walked along the cliffs above the harbor. [pause 0.3 s] The wind was so strong that we could hardly stand up. [pause 0.7 s] Later, we found a little cafe that sold fresh fish and chips. [pause 0.4 s] We sat by the window and watched the boats come in. [pause 1.1 s] The journey home was much quieter because we were both tired. [pause 0.4 s] I fell asleep before the train had even left the station. [pause 0.9 s] Since then, I have taken that train many times, [pause 0.3 s] but the first trip is still the one I remember best.
[pause 1.2 s] I remember it well because it was my first trip without my parents.
I think people want to see new places. [pause 0.5 s] Travel also helps us to learn about other cultures.
In some ways it is much easier now. [pause 0.4 s] Tickets are cheaper and we can book everything online.
[pause 0.7 s] but airports are often very crowded.

utterances.text: I live in a small house near the river. [pause 0.4 s] I have lived there for about six years. [pause 0.7 s] It is a quiet area with lots of trees.

I spend a lot of time in my garden. [pause 0.9 s] I grow tomatoes and beans every summer. [pause 0.4 s] At the weekend, I sometimes go fishing with my brother. [pause 1.1 s] Do you like animals? [pause 0.4 s] Yes, very much. [pause 0.5 s] We have an old dog who sleeps all day.
[pause 0.8 s] I also feed the birds in winter.

I would like to describe an old lighthouse on the coast near my town. [pause 0.5 s] It [withheld for audio check] museum. [pause 0.4 s] Inside there is a narrow staircase with about 200 steps. [pause 1.1 s] At the top, you can see the sea for many miles. [pause 0.3 s] I first visited it with my school when I was 10.

[pause 0.6 s] Our teacher told us stories about the ships that sank nearby. [pause 0.9 s] The building next to the tower was once the keeper's house. [pause 0.4 s] The keeper and his family lived there all year round. [pause 0.7 s] In winter, the storms were so bad that they could not leave for weeks. [pause 0.5 s] Now the house has a small cafe and a shop that sells old maps. [pause 0.8 s] I find it interesting because it shows how people lived in the past. [pause 1.1 s] Last summer, I took my nephew there for the first time.
[pause 0.4 s] For me, the lighthouse links my childhood with the history of my town. [pause 0.4 s] I still go there once or twice a year.
Many people are interested in history. [pause 0.4 s] Old buildings help us imagine life in another time.
[pause 0.7 s] Once an old building is gone, we cannot get it back.

definitions.definition: Seconds of voice-detector speech inside the answers; silences under 0.25 s count as speech.
definitions.caveat: Longer is not better; it depends on the questions.
definitions.how: voice detector; silences under 0.25 s count as speech

definitions.definition: Transcript syllables divided by the total answer time, pauses included.
definitions.caveat: Faster is not better; this describes how the answers were spoken, not how good they were. Syllables come from spelling.
definitions.how: syllables counted from spelling / total answer time

definitions.definition: Transcript syllables divided by the speaking time, pauses of 0.25 s or more left out.
definitions.caveat: Faster is not better; this describes how the answers were spoken, not how good they were. Syllables come from spelling.
definitions.how: syllables counted from spelling / speaking time

definitions.definition: Silences of 0.25 s or more inside the answers, per minute of answer time, from the voice detector.
definitions.caveat: Fewer pauses is not better: where a pause falls matters more than how many there are.
definitions.how: voice detector; count / minutes of answer time

definitions.definition: The mean length of the silent pauses of 0.25 s or more inside the answers.
definitions.caveat: Shorter is not better on its own.
definitions.how: voice detector; mean of the pauses of 0.25 s or more

definitions.definition: How many silent pauses inside the answers last 1 s or more.
definitions.caveat: A long pause can be planning; read it with the transcript.
definitions.how: voice detector; count

definitions.definition: How many silent pauses inside the answers last 0.5 s or more.
definitions.caveat: A view between the 0.25 s and 1 s counts.

definitions.definition: Percent of the silent pauses of 0.25 s or more whose words on both sides belong to one clause in spaCy's parse of the answer; the other pauses fall at a clause boundary.
definitions.caveat: Fewer is not better on its own: a pause inside a clause can be planning or a search for a word. The parser is trained on written text, so read each pause in the transcript.
definitions.how: grammar parser (spaCy) on the transcript; pauses from the voice detector

definitions.definition: Mean number of syllables between silent pauses of 0.25 s or more.
definitions.caveat: Longer is not better on its own; this describes how the answers were spoken, not how good they were.
definitions.how: syllables counted from spelling between pauses of 0.25 s or more

definitions.definition: Median time from a question's end to the first word of its answer; overlapping starts left out.
definitions.caveat: A short wait is not better: thinking before answering is normal.
definitions.how: question end to the answer's first word, from the speech model's word times

definitions.definition: How many answers started more than 10 s after their question ended; these are not in the median.
definitions.caveat: Check these by listening: the question may have been unclear.
definitions.how: question end to the answer's first word; count

definitions.definition: Hesitation sounds (um, uh, er and similar) per minute of answer time, as the transcript has them.
definitions.caveat: The recogniser may miss or add hesitation sounds; fewer is not better on its own.
definitions.how: speech model's transcript; count / minutes of answer time

definitions.definition: Transcript words other than hesitation sounds, per minute of answer time.
definitions.caveat: Kept out of the text for an AI chat, which might turn it into a band rule.

definitions.definition: The share of different words in each window of 50 words, averaged over all windows.
definitions.caveat: Higher variety is not better on its own; topic and answer length change it.
definitions.how: different words / 50 in each 50-word window, averaged

definitions.definition: Percent of content words that are not among the 2,000 most frequent English words. Names of people and places found by the grammar parser are left out, and a word counts as common when its base form is ("dishes" as "dish").
definitions.caveat: Rare is not good on its own; a rare word can be used wrongly.
definitions.how: wordfreq ranks of the word and its base form; names left out

definitions.definition: Percent of content words that are not among the 5,000 most frequent English words. Names of people and places found by the grammar parser are left out, and a word counts as common when its base form is ("dishes" as "dish").
definitions.caveat: Rare is not good on its own; a rare word can be used wrongly.
definitions.how: wordfreq ranks of the word and its base form; names left out

definitions.definition: Different linking words and phrases from Fluentfolio's list, divided by all uses of them.
definitions.caveat: More variety is not better on its own; a marker can be used wrongly.
definitions.how: different linking words / all their uses (list X03)

definitions.definition: Mean difference in length between neighbouring vowel stretches, as a percent of their mean length.
definitions.caveat: Context only: no norm says which values are better, and accents differ in rhythm.

definitions.definition: Standard deviation of the vowel stretch lengths, as a percent of their mean.
definitions.caveat: Context only: no norm says which values are better, and accents differ in rhythm.

definitions.definition: Percent of the time inside words that vowels take up.
definitions.caveat: Context only: no norm says which values are better, and accents differ in rhythm.

definitions.definition: Mean length of one vowel sound, from MFA's phone times.
definitions.caveat: Context only: no norm says which values are better, and accents differ in rhythm.

definitions.definition: Mean length of one consonant sound, from MFA's phone times.
definitions.caveat: Context only: no norm says which values are better, and accents differ in rhythm.

definitions.definition: The distance in semitones between the 20th and the 80th percentile of the candidate's pitch, over the answers with 10 s of voiced speech or more. Praat, SwiftF0 and openSMILE (when enabled) each measure it, and their values are combined with fixed weights.
definitions.caveat: Use it as it stands when the tools agree (within 1.0 semitone), only for broad statements when they are approximate (within 3.2), and not at all when they disagree. A wider range is not better on its own: voices, topics and styles differ.
definitions.how: Praat, SwiftF0 and openSMILE (when enabled), combined with fixed weights

definitions.definition: The middle of the candidate's pitch over the answers with 10 s of voiced speech or more, combined from the pitch tools in semitones and shown in Hz.
definitions.caveat: Use it as it stands when the tools agree (within 1.0 semitone), only for broad statements when they are approximate (within 3.2), and not at all when they disagree. Context only: a voice's pitch says nothing about how well it speaks.
definitions.how: Praat, SwiftF0 and openSMILE (when enabled), combined with fixed weights

definitions.definition: Stretches between pauses that last 2 s or more, with 1 s of pitch or more, whose pitch stays within 2 semitones (10th to 90th percentile). A semitone is the smallest step on a piano.
definitions.caveat: Heuristic threshold, not a norm: a list or a calm, even style can be flat.
definitions.how: heuristic: Praat pitch within 2 semitones for 2 s or more

definitions.definition: Stretches between pauses whose pitch rises by 2 semitones or more over their last 0.3 s of voice.
definitions.caveat: Heuristic thresholds, not a norm. Rising, falling and level endings are all normal in English; none is better.
definitions.how: heuristic: Praat pitch rises 2 semitones or more in the last 0.3 s

definitions.definition: Stretches between pauses whose pitch falls by 2 semitones or more over their last 0.3 s of voice.
definitions.caveat: Heuristic thresholds, not a norm. Rising, falling and level endings are all normal in English; none is better.
definitions.how: heuristic: Praat pitch falls 2 semitones or more in the last 0.3 s

definitions.definition: Stretches between pauses whose pitch moves by less than 2 semitones over their last 0.3 s of voice.
definitions.caveat: Heuristic thresholds, not a norm. Rising, falling and level endings are all normal in English; none is better.
definitions.how: heuristic: Praat pitch moves under 2 semitones in the last 0.3 s

definitions.definition: How much the loudness of the candidate's speech varies: its standard deviation divided by its mean, pauses left out (openSMILE, eGeMAPS).
definitions.caveat: Context only: the microphone, its distance and the room change it; more is not better on its own.
definitions.how: openSMILE eGeMAPS; standard deviation / mean, pauses left out

definitions.definition: Peaks in the loudness of the candidate's speech per second, pauses left out (openSMILE, eGeMAPS).
definitions.caveat: Context only: it follows syllables and stress, and the recording changes it.
definitions.how: openSMILE eGeMAPS; peaks per second, pauses left out

definitions.definition: Standard deviation of the pitch in semitones over the frames where Praat found a pitch.
definitions.caveat: More variation is not better on its own; voices and topics differ.

definitions.definition: Percent of the candidate's speech frames in which Praat found a pitch.
definitions.caveat: It depends on the sounds spoken and on the recording; context only.

definitions.definition: Mean change in length between neighbouring voice cycles, as a percent of the mean, over the voiced stretches of 1 s or more in the answer.
definitions.caveat: Context only: measured in connected speech, not on held vowels, so clinical norms do not apply.

definitions.definition: Mean change in loudness between neighbouring voice cycles, as a percent of the mean, over the voiced stretches of 1 s or more in the answer.
definitions.caveat: Context only: measured in connected speech, not on held vowels, so clinical norms do not apply.

definitions.definition: How much stronger the regular part of the voice is than its noise, in dB, over the voiced stretches of 1 s or more in the answer.
definitions.caveat: Context only: measured in connected speech, not on held vowels, so clinical norms do not apply.

definitions.definition: Mean frequency of the lowest resonance of the mouth and throat, over the voiced stretches of 1 s or more in the answer.
definitions.caveat: Context only: formants depend on the voice and on the vowels spoken.

definitions.definition: Mean frequency of the second resonance of the mouth and throat, over the voiced stretches of 1 s or more in the answer.
definitions.caveat: Context only: formants depend on the voice and on the vowels spoken.

definitions.definition: Mean frequency of the third resonance of the mouth and throat, over the voiced stretches of 1 s or more in the answer.
definitions.caveat: Context only: formants depend on the voice and on the vowels spoken.
